credit_ladder.session_to_tournament: session price credited toward the same tournament's pass until that tournament's final (₹29 + ₹50 = ₹79; ₹39 + ₹50 = ₹89)
credit_ladder.tournament_to_fts: tournament pass price credited (cap ₹99, one credit per account) toward the rest-of-season pass within 30 days (₹89 + ₹110 = ₹199)
credit_ladder.fts_to_season_2027: not a credit: loyalty price ₹349 instead of the assumed ₹399 list if bought by 15 Jan 2027
credit_ladder.precedence: exactly one price reduction per checkout: upgrade credit > segment offer > public promo; credits never stack
credit_ladder.identical_scope_checks: Sessions vs tournament (same event): 3 x ₹29 = ₹87 > ₹79 and 3 x ₹39 = ₹117 > ₹89/₹99, so buying sessions never beats the tournament pass from the third session; 2 sessions cost less than a pass and are the intended entry. Tournaments vs rest-of-season (same 7-week scope): 2 passes = ₹158-₹178 < ₹199 < 3 passes = ₹237-₹267, so only three-or-more event buyers save. Ladder totals equal direct prices (₹29+₹50 = ₹79; ₹89+₹110 = ₹199), so no path undercuts a direct purchase.

cohorts.note: Pathway probabilities for a tournament-pass entrant; repeat+upgrade = 60% base reflects the case's 60-65% repeat-purchase observation (lower bound, window unspecified).

renewal_2027_loyalty.note: assumptions for newly acquired lower-intent cohorts; the case's ~90% season renewal is not applied to them

cohorts.note_2028: case-informed (~90% season renewal, CF7) applied only to customers who already renewed once; 2028 season bought Jan 2028 within the rights horizon

cannibalisation.note_a: share of would-be FTS-direct buyers who enter via a tournament pass and never upgrade
cannibalisation.note_b: share of upgraders who would have bought 3+ tournament passes at full price
cannibalisation.note_c: share of loyalty-price renewers who would have renewed at ₹399
